Subject: Request: sandboxing/bridged-tenant footprint + CAIQ/SOC2 crosswalk

Rishi,

Thanks for taking this on — BlueRiver Security is preparing our SOC 2 scoping and SIG review for an upcoming procurement round. We need a concise architecture bundle that explains how Redwood provisions isolation between Dedicated and Private deployments when customers require a bridged/sandboxing model (i.e., customer-managed VPC peering vs controlled on-prem edge). Specifically, could you provide: 

- A network diagram that shows control plane vs data plane separation for both Dedicated and Private modes (calls out peering, transit, and egress paths).
- A short one-page narrative (executive + technical) describing how tenant fencing is enforced and where the blast radius is bounded.
- A CAIQ crosswalk (mapping of relevant CAIQ questions to Redwood evidence artifacts) focused on network/topology items.
- Typical ACL examples and at-rest/control-plane key handling notes (redacted).

Timing: our SOC 2 auditor kickoff is next week (2026-01-19). If you can share a draft by EOD 2026-01-14 that would be ideal. If helpful, can schedule a 30-min technical sync.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Dawson
CISO, BlueRiver Health

We'll mark the diagram with the control-plane breakout, KV/HSM boundaries, and the typical KV cache duration that affects leakage window.

I'll start assembling the initial diagram and CAIQ mapping and loop you in on Drive.

Rishi / team — quick technical clarifications I'll include in the attachment: bridged_fence_v1.png (attached) — highlights below so Emma/Oliver can review before the call:

- Control plane: runs in Redwood-managed VPCs in our control plane subnet; control plane egress is via dedicated NAT with egress logging and enforced egress policies. Customers on Dedicated are given a control-plane endpoint (mTLS) that authenticates via client certs; Private deployments optionally run a local control-plane proxy that forwards only auth+control metadata.
- Data plane: customer workloads run in either Redwood Dedicated GPU pools (isolated tenant pools) or in customer-managed VPCs for Private. For \"Peered Dedicated\" we enforce a deny-by-default routing posture, with explicit /32 routes for service endpoints and a thin proxy for metrics/heartbeat.
- KV / secrets: keys for tokenization and model encryption are stored in HSM-backed KMS (per-customer CMK where requested). Control-plane operations do not have direct access to encrypted model weights or customer content in the customer VPC unless explicitly requested for troubleshooting under strict audit.

I'll attach ACL snippets (network_acl_snippets.txt) showing the minimal set we typically add for peering; happy to redact anything you request.

Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Infrastructure Security | Redwood Inference

Emma / Oliver — attaching the draft bundle as requested: soc2_network_map_v2.pdf, caiq_crosswalk_v2.xlsx, network_acl_snippets.txt. Drive link here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_drawio_networks

Executive summary (short):
- Isolation model: Redwood provides a layered tenancy fence composed of (1) physical/gpu pool isolation for Dedicated, (2) VPC-level peering with strict route controls for peered Dedicated, and (3) optional on-prem edge proxies for Private deployments. Control plane traffic is strictly segregated and authenticated via mTLS and client-side certs; control plane egress is restricted to a small set of telemetry and artifact endpoints and logged centrally.
- Evidence linkage: CAIQ items in the provided spreadsheet point to specific artifacts (flow logs, peering ACL exports, KMS CMK policy snippets, and control-plane proxy config). Rows flagged as \"high-priority\" are recommended for SOC 2 scoping.

Notes on differences between patterns included in the spreadsheet: 
- Peered Dedicated vs Edge-bridged Private: the main variance is the locus of egress control and where the first network enforcement point lives (Redwood edge vs customer edge). Both support HSM-backed keys and per-tenant CMKs on request.

Open items for you before finalizing: 
1) Please confirm whether you need the KMS CMK policy text redacted or a sanitized example.
2) Any preference for inclusion of packet-capture level evidence or would flow logs be sufficient for your auditor?

Attachments: soc2_network_map_v2.pdf (diagram), caiq_crosswalk_v2.xlsx (crosswalk), network_acl_snippets.txt (ACL examples).

Thanks — can revise and finalize post-sync.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
